independentSourceInventory.pixelFacts: One top rectangular two-region sample with full vertical divider, n-form left glyph and p-form right glyph. Each external lead contacts the midpoint of its outer side, not the divider. No bulk-charge signs.
independentSourceInventory.comparison: Sample division, region ordering and both side contacts match the pixels.

independentSourceInventory.pixelFacts: Two complete circular meter outlines. The A-form meter is in the upper-right series branch, with top and bottom contacts. The V-form meter bridges the middle left and right junctions, with left and right circle contacts. No internal scale, ticks, needle or measured value.
independentSourceInventory.comparison: Both full 360-degree outlines remain intact, not incomplete arcs. Wire ends meet circle contours and do not cross instrument labels. V remains across the sample-plus-A upper branch, not silently rewired across the sample alone.

independentSourceInventory.pixelFacts: Exactly three filled junction dots: middle left on the V branch, middle right below A on the V branch, and lower right at the fixed resistor lead. Middle dots are on one horizontal branch; both right dots are on the same vertical trunk.
independentSourceInventory.comparison: Exactly these three visible points remain. No dot or connection is added where the sample-left/wiper feed passes above the separate fixed-left resistor supply leg.

independentSourceInventory.pixelFacts: The sample-left/V-left node descends, turns right, then drops as a downward arrow onto the top interior of one horizontal resistor rectangle. The resistor has distinct left and right fixed terminals; the wiper is its separate third contact.
independentSourceInventory.comparison: The wiper tip contacts the top border within the resistor, points down, and is not substituted by a lead to the fixed-left terminal. Both fixed-end legs remain.

independentSourceInventory.pixelFacts: Separate hollow lower-left and lower-right terminal marks with minus below the left and plus below the right. The fixed-left resistor lead goes down the left outer leg to minus. The fixed-right lead joins the right trunk, which continues to plus. The top sample-right lead goes through A to this trunk. There is an open supply gap, not battery plates or a shorting line.
independentSourceInventory.comparison: Every source branch/bend remains. Both terminals are hollow and distinct, their polarity is preserved, and no new line spans the source gap.

scientificMeaning.finding: The right positive supply reaches the p side through the series ammeter; the n side reaches the adjustable wiper on the supply resistor. This is the forward-bias arrangement in both complete languages. A measures sample-branch current; V is across the entire sample-plus-A branch, exactly as in the source. The lesson makes no precision claim that V alone isolates a nonideal ammeter's voltage drop. No carrier-direction arrow, bulk-charge sign, measured apparatus value or rectified waveform is invented.

modernDecisions: Modern n/p are prose-defined region identities; literal source homograph identity remains unresolved.
Modern A follows the circular series instrument's ammeter meaning, not an assertion of Latin rather than Cyrillic glyph identity.
The slanted hollow source terminals are regularized to circles without changing their open status or polarity.
The source is schematic: exact modern right angles, circle radii and component spacing are drafting choices, not apparatus measurements.
